subject: Order form - discount waterfall & escrow language redline
messages:
From: Alice Winters <alice.winters@orbitalhealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@orbitalhealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial redlines – order form and pricing exhibit (DH-2026-019)

Sean, thanks for the demo last week — Orbital Health is excited to move forward. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the order form and attached a redline with a few asks we need to resolve before we can sign. High level: 1) They pushed back on the unconditional tiered discount waterfall — they want a cap on cumulative discounts and a floor on minimum monthly committed spend. 2) They requested an escrow mechanism for overage credits if Redwood changes billing metrics mid-term. 3) They proposed a 90-day true-up window and a unilateral audit right for our billing metrics.

I've attached the PDF with inline comments and an XLS with their proposed waterfall math. Can you confirm who on your side will pick this up? Procurement would like an updated redline this week if possible.

Thanks,
Alice Winters
Head of Procurement
Orbital Health
procurement@orbitalhealth.com

Attachments: OrderForm_DH-2026-019_redline.pdf, Pricing-Exhibit-Waterfall.xlsx

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Initial redlines – order form and pricing exhibit (DH-2026-019)

Team — forwarding Alice's email and the attachments. Quick thoughts before we reply to Orbital:

- Discount waterfall: they're asking for a cap on cumulative concession. We typically allow a stair-step limit tied to committed spend; legal wants to avoid an open-ended escrow.
- Escrow/credits: Orbital wants escrow for credits in case we change billing metrics mid-term — that's atypical for us but doable as a transitional remedy (time-boxed).
- True-up & audit: 90 days is long; we can offer 45 days and a single audit per year, mutually agreed auditor.

Marissa — can you draft a customer-facing counter that keeps our standard protections (cap on aggregate discounts, defined true-up mechanics) but offers a concession on a one-time escrow hold with release milestones? Karthik/Laura, legal language suggestions appreciated.

I'll loop Orbital once we have a clean counter.

—Sean
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Forwarded attachments: OrderForm_DH-2026-019_redline.pdf, Pricing-Exhibit-Waterfall.xlsx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alice Winters <alice.winters@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Initial redlines – order form and pricing exhibit (DH-2026-019)

Alice — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. We've reviewed and prepared a counterproposal attached. Summary of key points in plain language: 

1) Discount waterfall & cap: We can accept a cap on cumulative discount exposure (expressed as a percentage of committed annual spend) rather than an uncapped waterfall. Proposed cap: 18% of committed spend per contract year, with a reconciliation at true-up. This keeps your economics predictable while limiting our downside.

2) Minimum monthly commitment (floor): We will set a soft floor (monthly minimum) that triggers a true-up at year-end rather than an immediate penalty. The floor amount and forgiveness window are in the attached pricing exhibit.

3) Escrow for overage credits: We are willing to create a short-term escrow account for disputed credit reserves for up to 60 days after a metric change, with escrow release tied to documentation of billing logic and mutual sign-off. We are not comfortable with an open-ended escrow.

4) True-up and audit: We propose a 45-day true-up window after month/quarter close and one audit per 12 months with a mutually agreed third-party auditor; Redwood covers auditor fees unless the audit shows >5% misreporting.

Please see the attached: "OrderForm_DH-2026-019_redline.pdf" (clean counter with inline notes) and "Pricing-Exhibit-Waterfall.xlsx" (example math). If these look reasonable, can we schedule a 30-minute call Thurs to finalize?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: OrderForm_DH-2026-019_redline.pdf

From: Orbital Legal <legal@orbitalhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:39:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Initial redlines – order form and pricing exhibit (DH-2026-019)

Marissa — thanks for the counter. A few technical/legal points we need clarified before committing to a call: 

- Your proposed 18% cap: please confirm whether that cap is applied per contract year or to the life of the agreement (we require per-year clarity).
- Escrow mechanics: Orbital requires (i) a formula describing how the escrow amount is calculated, (ii) an independent escrow agent (we can propose one), and (iii) an automatic release schedule if no dispute is raised within 60 days. Your draft references "documentation" — Orbital wants the definition of acceptable documentation spelled out (usage reports with hash/IDs, summary of billing logic, and a contact for technical reconciliation).
- Billing metric changes: Orbital insists on a 180-day notice and a transitional credit equal to the delta in projected run-rate for 90 days unless mutually agreed otherwise.

We are okay moving forward if Redwood can accept per-year cap treatment, provide a clearer escrow formula in the pricing exhibit, and define acceptable reconciliation evidence. Please provide a precise clause we can mark up.

Regards,
Kendall Price
Senior Counsel, Orbital Health
legal@orbitalhealth.com

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Alice Winters <alice.winters@orbitalhealth.com>, Kendall Price <legal@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Initial redlines – order form and pricing exhibit (DH-2026-019)

Thanks, Kendall & Alice — appreciate the specificity. We're aligned on the big picture and can accept per-contract-year application of the cumulative discount cap. Attached is a short addendum we propose to insert into the Pricing Exhibit describing: 

- Cap: "Cumulative Discount Cap" equals 18% of the then-current Contract Year committed spend, applied on an annual basis and reset at the start of each Contract Year.
- Escrow formula: escrow amount equals the lesser of (a) projected 90-day revenue delta caused by a billing metric change, or (b) 5% of the then-current Contract Year committed spend; escrow held with ACME Escrow Services and released per the schedule in the exhibit unless a written dispute is lodged within 60 calendar days.
- Acceptable reconciliation evidence: monthly usage reports exported from Redwood's billing system including request IDs, timestamps, and top-line usage summary; both parties will maintain a shared reconciliation spreadsheet for transparency.

We will update the PDF and XLS and share the new redline (OrderForm_DH-2026-019_redline_v2.pdf). If that works, we can book Thurs 30-minute call to sign off. If Orbital prefers a different escrow agent or tweaks to the release schedule, let's surface them on the call.

—Sean
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_DH-2026-019_redline_v2.pdf, Pricing-Exhibit-Waterfall.xlsx
